record.paper_title: Topological Open Problems in the Geometry of Banach Spaces
record.original_question: Are descriptive Banach spaces exactly the σ-fragmented Banach spaces, or is one of these two classes strictly larger? In this setting, a descriptive Banach space is a Banach space whose norm topology has a network that is the countable union of subfamilies which are isolated or discrete in their union for the weak topology.

evidence.quote: the norm topology has a network N that can be written as a countable union of subfamilies, N = ∪∞ n=1Nn, where every one of the subfamilies Nn is a discrete family in its union ∪{N : N ∈ Nn} endowed with the weak topology, i.e., it is an isolated subfamily for the weak topology. No example is known of a Banach space with this kind of network, which is called a descriptive Banach space, and without equivalent Kadec norm
Question 3. Is there any gap between the classes of descriptive Banach spaces and that of σ-fragmented Banach spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a Banach space, and let $\tau$ denote its norm topology and $w$ its weak topology. A family $\mathcal{N}$ of subsets of $X$ is called a network for $\tau$ if every $\tau$-open set is a union of members of $\mathcal{N}$. A family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $X$ is said to be isolated (or discrete in its union) for the weak topology if, equipping $Y := \bigcup\{F : F \in \mathcal{F}\}$ with the relative weak topology, every point of $Y$ has a $w$-open neighborhood meeting at most one member of $\mathcal{F}$.

Call $X$ a descriptive Banach space if $\tau$ admits a network $\mathcal{N} = \bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty} \mathcal{N}_n$ such that, for each $n$, the subfamily $\mathcal{N}_n$ is isolated for the weak topology in its union.

Call $X$ a $\sigma$-fragmented Banach space (with respect to the norm) if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a decomposition $X = \bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty} X_n^\varepsilon$ such that, for each $n$ and each nonempty subset $A \subseteq X_n^\varepsilon$, there exists a weakly open set $U \subseteq X$ with $U \cap A \neq \emptyset$ and $\|\cdot\|$-diameter of $U \cap A$ less than $\varepsilon$.

Question: Does the class of descriptive Banach spaces coincide with the class of $\sigma$-fragmented Banach spaces, or is one of these classes strictly larger than the other?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the standard literature on σ-fragmentability and descriptive Banach spaces (Jayne–Namioka–Rogers, Cascales–Namioka, Oncina–Raja) and various surveys of open problems in Banach space geometry, but no source found explicitly settles whether the two classes coincide. The status appears to remain unresolved, but no definitive source was located confirming it as still open as of the search date.

status_evidence.title: σ-fragmentable Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper introducing σ-fragmentability of Banach spaces, with no resolution of equivalence to descriptiveness.
status_evidence.claim: The notions are studied separately in the literature without an established coincidence.

status_evidence.title: Fragmentability in Banach spaces: Interaction of topologies
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-type article on fragmentability and descriptive properties; does not announce a solution to the gap question.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution to the gap between descriptive and σ-fragmented Banach spaces is reported.
